## Q43 independent privacy re-review — ACCEPT @ `e78d371`

**Scope reviewed:** `web/src/features/contacts/journey.ts`, `web/src/features/privacy/consent.ts`, README, and all tests. Diff confirmed: 8 files, all under `web/src/features/contacts|privacy/**` + matching tests. No credentials, no storage, no UI, no transport ownership — the lane boundaries in the README hold.

**Declared validation, reproduced independently** (Node 24.17.0, detached worktree at e78d371):
- `node --test web/tests/contacts/*.test.mjs web/tests/privacy/*.test.mjs` → 19 pass, 3 skipped (persisted, by design)
- `node web/tests/contacts/run-persisted.mjs` → isolated Unix-socket Postgres, strict tsc clean, 3/3 persisted integration tests pass against real backend routes with real signed tokens. The persisted scenarios are the strongest evidence here: narrowed consent denies maps while incident flow survives; fresh browser instances observe trip vs standing revoke independently from SQL state (not local flags); a forged local driver view holding a contact JWT is refused resolve by the backend; a stranger token sees nothing.

**Independent probes (8, not in the branch's suite — all pass):**
1. A pending command blocks every other command; the blocked one never reaches the transport.
2. An uncertain command blocks even a different-kind command; explicit retry reuses the exact idempotency key.
3. Revocation is never blocked by an uncertain command, conceals first, and discards the stale retry — the correct precedence.
4. In-flight reads are aborted by revoke; subsequent reads always get a fresh, non-aborted controller.
5. Cross-trip incident payloads never render even when otherwise well-formed.
6. `getState()` clones are deeply isolated — mutating invitation/receipts/location on the snapshot cannot touch live state.
7. A malformed resolve response keeps the incident concealed and never marks it resolved.
8. A hinted invitation with driver==contact or another contactId can never issue an accept command.

**Privacy posture verified:** conceal-before-revoke (standing and trip), epoch+sequence invalidation kills late responses after any role/identity/trip change, 401/403/404 on any command clears all protected caches (401 also drops the session), acceptance narrows scopes client-side and is never treated as authorization (`currentAuthorization: 'requires-server-check'` throughout), ambiguous writes never auto-replay, contact acknowledgement/actions never resolve an incident, driver-only resolution is enforced locally AND proven server-side in the persisted suite.

No privacy or correctness findings. Ship-ready from the privacy lane; integration remains Q44's call.

## Q43 re-review of current head — ACCEPT @ `5c15183` (supersedes my e78d371 scoped pass)

Delta reviewed: `e78d371..5c15183` = `b95bdba` (fix: preserve unknown writes after refused retries) + `5c15183` (docs: contact-route readiness inventory). 3 files, 124 insertions.

**Q45's lost-revoke → same-key-409 bug: CONFIRMED FIXED.**
- `journey.ts`: a failure on a *retried* command (`existingKey !== undefined`) now stays `uncertain` regardless of the refusal's status — a 409/4xx on attempt 2 is evidence about that attempt, not proof attempt 1 didn't commit. First-attempt definitive 4xx still classifies `rejected`. Correct distinction.
- Read-path denials (403/404) now call `invalidate(true)`: data is concealed but the unresolved write outcome + its retry path survive. Correct — a read denial must not erase an unresolved write.
- 401 anywhere drops the session AND the retry (`retry = null`), so an unknown-outcome command can never replay into another identity. Correct.
- Write-path denials still conceal everything first. Revocation precedence over stuck commands is preserved.

**Verification at exact 5c15183** (Node 24.17.0, detached worktree):
- Declared suite: 21/21 unit pass (was 19 at e78; +2 fix regression tests), 3/3 persisted integration pass against isolated Unix-socket Postgres with real signed tokens; strict tsc clean inside the runner.
- My 8 original e78 probes re-run against this head: all still pass (no regression in pending/uncertain exclusivity, abort semantics, cross-trip rejection, clone isolation, malformed-resolve concealment, invitation-refusal).
- 6 new probes targeting this fix, all pass: (1) Q45's exact repro — lost revoke + same-key 409 → stays uncertain, reads blocked, 3rd attempt resolves; (2) first-attempt 409 stays `rejected`, never reclassified; (3) same-session read denial conceals data but preserves the unknown outcome; (4) retried-write 401 drops session + retry permanently; (5) uncertain write never blocks revocation of any grant; (6) documents the one residual edge below.

**Non-blocking observation (not a defect for this head):** a session/trip switch discards an unresolved uncertain write client-side (`invalidate()` without preserve). Data stays concealed and the server remains the enforcement backstop, so there is no leak — but the UI forgets the outcome was unknown. If a future UI surfaces operation history, consider preserving the uncertain marker across trip switches the same way read-denials now do.

**Docs (5c15183):** the contact-route readiness inventory and the minimal retrieval request to lane41 are accurate against the backend I reviewed at `c752de8` — recipient invitation detail and shared-trip discovery are correctly identified as the two missing reads; PR65's driver-only trip list is correctly called out as not satisfying contact discovery. Cosmetic nit only: two missing spaces in README prose ("including409", "explicit1–300").

Ship-ready from the privacy lane at this head. My earlier e78d371 ACCEPT is scoped/superseded; this verdict covers `5c15183`.

**Q59 narrow source review — P2, nonblocking helper issue at exact head `e2c1e677cf3ec3fa9c7f91529b082ab5b8ff91e6`.** This is not a full review or acceptance of the newly added UI.

`web/src/features/contacts/journey.ts:74–81`, exported `locationAge(snapshot, nowMs)`, adds `nowMs - Date.parse(snapshot.readAt)` to server age. `readAt` is server wall time, but there is no exported same-client receipt or documented server-clock anchor for `nowMs`. Passing client wall time therefore changes the age according to device/server offset: server age120s + actual elapsed120s gives240s aligned,180s with a client60s behind,300s with one60s ahead. A backward client step can reduce the returned age while nowMs remains >=readAt. Also a capturedAt300ms ahead that the backend accepts/clamps to age0 yields null solely due to capturedAt>readAt.

The [preserved reproducer and raw observations](https://github.com/Bimbi-Dev/andes-hackathon/blob/16d51a1873c54fdc302c5cdd002b9fa2bb851e89/docs/reviews/pr53/README.md#follow-on-source-age-bridge-finding) first established this at21cd50a. I rechecked the unchanged helper against this current head using Node24.17.0 and ran its existing contact/privacy suites: **22/22 pass**. These synthetic arithmetic probes are not browser/device or signed-backend evidence.

**Current consumer boundary:** `routes.tsx`'s Location renders raw `fact.ageMs` and `fact.freshness`; the ES/PT-BR labels explicitly say “in that read” and disclose that it is a prior observation. No production feature source calls `locationAge` at this head. `serverFreshnessAtRead`, live:false and requires-server-check also remain intact. I am not alleging a live/safe UI claim or an authorization failure.

Owner51's narrow correction can either retain server age solely as-of-read, or require an explicit same-client receipt/elapsed anchor and document its clock/reset limits. Do not subtract server readAt from an unqualified client clock or copy the retired PR53 projector. Keep the positive aligned control, offset/backward-step counterexamples and backend-accepted +300ms capture.

Original reviewer43 explicitly concurs with this P2 and its display-only boundary; their prior scoped privacy ACCEPT is unchanged, and this is not a privacy merge blocker. Owner fix/contract clarification and reviewer43 confirmation of the corrected immutable SHA remain pending. No finding is marked fixed/ACCEPT by Q59, no whole-PR approval is submitted and no merge or product issue closure is implied.
